title: Content-encoding codecs and Message decode/encode callpath
answers: How does Message.content decode the body?
body:
- Registries: `custom_decode` / `custom_encode` dicts at bottom of `mitmproxy/net/encoding.py` (keys none, identity, gzip, deflate, deflateraw, br, zstd). Add a new codec by adding a function pair and registering in both dicts.
- `encoding.decode()`/`encode()` try the custom dict, on KeyError fall back to stdlib `codecs.decode/encode` (text codecs like utf8); failures are re-raised as ValueError.
- `http.py:Message.get_content(strict=True)`: reads content-encoding header → `encoding.decode(self.raw_content, ce)`; str result → ValueError("Invalid Content-Encoding"); strict=False swallows and returns raw bytes.
- `Message.set_content`: `encoding.encode(value, ce or "identity")` → raw_content; invalid encoding deletes the header; updates content-length unless transfer-encoding present.
- `Message.decode()` = get_content, pop header, set content. `Message.encode(enc)` sets header then `self.content = self.raw_content` (encodes existing raw bytes, no decode first).
- get_text/set_text use `infer_content_encoding` (net/http/headers.py) for charset, then encoding.decode/encode.
